target.role: fresh whole-journey belonging and placement discovery for STRANGE GAIT
target.position: Whole journey: before the opener, between every non-protected pair, or after the tail. Preserve only Transparency → When We Froze and When We Froze → Stardancer; Truth in Noise → Transparency remains available.
target.purpose: Test two current or emerging constructions, two overlooked polymetric or syncopated catalogue cuts, and one lower-tempo metric reset. Character change is allowed; admission still requires purposeful transition, local-run and long-form effect.

sourceWindows: CURRENT 2026 / BLACK MAGIC RECS: https://blackmagicrecs.bandcamp.com/album/r-e-s-e-t — all four tracks were screened. Omnitron — R.E.S.E.T. was retained from the official exact-track description of a form that twists and snarls above 140 BPM through acid/electro synths, vocal bursts and locked drum programming.

CURRENT 2026 / WAS WOTSCH: https://waswotsch.bandcamp.com/album/local-lifeforms — all five tracks were screened. Michal Ho — Quamomibass was retained from the official exact-track description of an experimental, polymetric opener referencing the artist's drum-and-bass alter ego. The prose spells the title Quaomibass while the track listing spells Quamomibass; the request uses the listed title and preserves the discrepancy.

OVERLOOKED CATALOGUE / DOR BACHOV: https://dorbachov.bandcamp.com/album/invexis-morphium-ep — all four tracks were screened. Invexis — RS was retained from the official exact-track description of syncopated, complex motion and late-1990s groove science.

OVERLOOKED CATALOGUE / BERCEUSE HEROIQUE: https://ra.co/reviews/23275 — all four tracks on Hodge's Exogenesis EP were screened through Resident Advisor's review. Hodge — Night Run was retained from the exact-track description of a polyrhythmic construction with bright melodies and a rolling bassline.

ADJACENT / SELF-RELEASED: https://syntrovert.bandcamp.com/album/polymetrik-ep — both tracks were screened. syntrovert — Polymetrik was retained from the official exact-track description of a polyrhythmic and polymetric arrangement at 126 BPM.

ADDITIONAL WINDOWS: Stefan Goldmann's Alluvium, Jock Club's Bruk In The Days, Gynoid Audio's Grind, forthcoming Astel releases, current Bandcamp electronic roundups and adjacent label catalogues were screened. Their evidence was release-level, pre-release, insufficiently exact or weaker than the five ranked leads.
explorationReceipt.approximateInspectedScope: Approximately 46 named tracks and releases across current releases, adjacent/emerging artists and labels, and overlooked catalogue windows; metadata and attributed descriptions only, with zero audio auditions.
exclusions: All 14 canonical identities, active placement-specific rejects and every untriggered PARKED revisit were excluded. Exact identities and primary discovery lanes retained in Runs 53–71 were not recycled.
The protected internal handoffs Transparency → When We Froze and When We Froze → Stardancer remain unavailable; Truth in Noise → Transparency and every other boundary remain available.
No lead was promoted for recency, reputation, genre, novelty, title or technical cleverness. Album-level claims were not converted into exact-track behaviour.

Energy, density, space, hypnosis, emotional effect, perceived pulse, phrase structure, harmonic relation and mixability remain unknown. The source-reported 126 BPM for Polymetrik and above-140 range for R.E.S.E.T. are evidence, not flow verdicts.
rankedLeadSummary: 1. Omnitron — R.E.S.E.T.: strongest current exact structural case, officially described as twisting and snarling while its drums lock motion above 140 BPM.
2. Michal Ho — Quamomibass: strongest emerging polymetric case, with an official exact-track description and a preserved source-title discrepancy.
3. Invexis — RS: strongest overlooked syncopated-techno case, officially described as complex and kinetically mobile.
4. Hodge — Night Run: overlooked adjacent catalogue cut with an exact review documenting a polyrhythmic construction.
5. syntrovert — Polymetrik: lower-tempo exact metric experiment whose reported 126 BPM makes it a meaningful reset hypothesis rather than an automatic veto.
